title: Faz 6 two-person integrity primitive — CommandEnvelope v3 co_approver_actor + co_approver_signature wire fields

title: Faz 2 D-2 partial — mlock pin process pages in RAM via mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE) (memfd_secret + panic_zeroize registry land in #310 + #311)
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-2 + ADR-018 §7 + ADR-019 §5 in-process hardening. Pre-Batch-#309 the process_hardening module installed prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (Layer B — kernel-level coredump suppression) + panic-abort hook (Layer D — no destructor unwinding on panic) but the master keystore pages had NO mlockall guarantee — kernel could page secret bytes (master key, derived per-purpose keys, envelope signature material) to swap under memory pressure. An attacker with post-reboot forensic access to the swap partition (eMMC dump, cloud-VM hypervisor escape) could extract the master key from a paged-out copy even though the in-RAM copy was correctly drop-zeroized. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::mlock submodule wrapping mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE) — locks every current page AND every future allocation including async stack frames + heap regrowth. Idempotent (kernel ignores second call), structured error taxonomy (NotPermitted/InsufficientLimit/TemporaryFailure/UnknownErrno/UnsupportedPlatform) discriminating the EPERM/ENOMEM/EAGAIN/other errno classes, MlockState{locked_current, locked_future} return shape captures the actual posture for audit emission, proc_self_vm_locked_bytes() audit accessor parses /proc/self/status VmLck for runtime verification + future observability metrics.
